title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-19
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > CD > EAC > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a 1970 show highlighted by an epic Dark Star, stellar St. Stephen/NFA sequence and a raucous Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The matrix‑derived SBD capture is crisp and clear, with only occasional minor hiccups, letting the band’s inspired 1970 performance shine.  Highlights include a transcendent Dark Star, tight transitions into St. Stephen, Not Fade Away, Darkness jam and a wild Lovelight featuring Pig Pen’s infamous rap.  Overall the set flows brilliantly and showcases top‑form playing from all members.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 40 detailed reviews, virtually all 5‑star, praise both the musical performance (standout Dark Star, tight jams) and the technical quality (excellent SBD sound). Minor complaints are isolated and do not affect the overall high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crystal‑clear mix with superb instrument separation; a few reviewers note tiny scratches at the 16‑min mark and occasional peripheral percussion that sits forward, but overall no dropouts or muffiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set builds from a soaring Dark Star into St. Stephen, then erupts through Not Fade Away and the Darkness jam before seguing into China Cat and a raucous Lovelight – a seamless, high‑energy arc praised by multiple reviewers.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is described as perfect on Dark Star, with an early feedback squeal and “beast”‑like playing on the China Cat solo; his work in the ‘Feeling Groovy’ jam is called transcendent.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass line underpins the set solidly; one reviewer notes his “bomb” opening St. Stephen, indicating a strong, supportive low end.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm/lead contributions are highlighted – dual‑guitar tones on China Cat and an energetic lead stretch in the NFA/Darkness sections receive high praise.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums lock tightly with Garcia’s guitar throughout, described as a perfect match; the overall rhythmic drive is lauded.
